findings.title: Unconditional /100 is wrong for currencies not using 2 minor digits
findings.evidence: The function accepts any `currency` but always divides by 100 before formatting; e.g. `formatMoney(1000, 'JPY')` yields 10 yen instead of 1000, and 3-minor-unit currencies (KWD/BHD) would be off by 10x.
findings.recommendation: Derive the minor-unit divisor from the currency (e.g. via Intl.NumberFormat(...).resolvedOptions().maximumFractionDigits) or document/enforce that only 2-decimal currencies are accepted and reject others.

findings.title: Floating-point division can misformat large cent amounts
findings.evidence: `amountCents / 100` is a double, and since `Number.isSafeInteger` admits values up to 2^53-1, values like 9007199254740991 / 100 cannot be represented exactly, so rounding at a .xx5 boundary can display the wrong cent.
findings.recommendation: Format the integer part and the fractional cents separately, or cap the accepted range to an amount where the 2-decimal rounding is provably exact; add an edge-case test near the safe-integer limit.
